abstract: Fix $A>0$, $0<\eta\le1$, and $b\ge0$. We prove that there are constants $K$ and $X_0$ depending only on these parameters such that the following holds for every signed rational start $x$ of magnitude at least $X_0$ and reduced odd denominator at most $|x|^b$. Put $n=\lfloor\log_2|x|\rfloor$. If the first $Kn$ shortcut Collatz parity bits have at most $An$ distinct length-$n$ factors, some state within those $Kn$ steps has magnitude less than $|x|^\eta$. To prove this, we mark the terminal factor and all branching vertices of a finite Rauzy graph. Short excursions produce a bounded list of rational affine coordinates. A common integer clears the moving denominators outside $2$ and $3$ while preserving a strict gap in real growth rates. The $S$-unit equation theorem and two applications of the Subspace Theorem with fixed rational forms use this gap to contradict the independence of a basis of coordinates. Applying the finite theorem at minima of late tails gives $P(n)/n\to\infty$ for every aperiodic shortcut orbit of a signed rational with odd denominator, where $P(n)$ counts all length-$n$ parity factors. This includes every divergent positive-integer orbit. The constants are qualitative. The finite conclusion is conditional on the local factor count, and the infinite conclusion leaves the existence of divergent positive-integer orbits open.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: Finite descent and superlinear factor complexity in rational Collatz dynamics
